physical_harm: Five persons were done to death by inflicting blows with swords, gandasis and sticks
number_of_offences: 17 persons were convicted out of which 6 were sentenced to death and 11 to life imprisonment; the rest were acquitted
premeditation_planning: The accused formed an unlawful assembly with a common object to put an end to the lives of the deceased persons
motive: Revenge for the murder of Ram Narayan's son
key_evidence_accepted: The witnesses have lost their father, husband and a relative, and they have mentioned about the weapons used, the assault made and the parts of the body where injuries were inflicted. Their evidence is found to be reliable and credible, with only minor discrepancies.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the witnesses as credible and reliable, noting that they were victims of the crime and had a motive to seek justice, not to falsely implicate others. Their testimony was not discarded as untrustworthy.
custody_duration: almost spent thirteen years in custody
trial_duration: The crime took place on 28th and 29th June, 2001. The trial judgment was delivered on 3.4.2002 and 21.09.2002. The High Court decision was on 02.06.2005. The Supreme Court decision was on APRIL 22, 2013.
legal_representation: Sushil Kumar Jain, Puneet Jain, Anurag Gohil, Pratibha Jain for the Appellants. lmtiaz Ahmed, Naghma lmtiaz, Milind Kumar for the Respondent.
investigation_status: FIR lodged at 6.45 a.m. on 29.6.2001. Charge-sheets submitted on different dates before the Judicial Magistrate, Digod. Case committed to the Court of Session.
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal by High Court. High Court: Partly allowed appeals, acquitted some accused and converted death sentences to life imprisonment. Supreme Court: Dismissed all appeals, upheld High Court's decision.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the crime was a result of revenge for the murder of Ram Narayan's son, and that the accused formed an unlawful assembly with a common object to kill the deceased persons. The FIR delay was explained as due to trauma and fear, and the witnesses' testimony was deemed reliable.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court's acquittals were reasonable, as the evidence was inconclusive and there were discrepancies. The High Court properly extended the benefit of doubt to some accused persons, and the death sentence was excessive given the circumstances.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the death penalty should be imposed only in the rarest of rare cases, and that life imprisonment is the rule with death sentence as an exception.
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684; Machhi Singh and Others v. State of Punjab (1983) 3 SCC 470; State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta (2012) 1 SCC 602; Ram Pal v. State of U.P. (2003) 7 SCC 141
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the totality of the circumstances, including the gravity of the crime, the accused's prolonged custody, and the fact that similarly placed persons received life sentences. The Court found that life imprisonment was not inadequate and that the circumstances did not justify the death penalty.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The accused persons had spent almost thirteen years in custody, and similarly placed persons had been given life sentences. The Court considered the trauma and fear of the witnesses and the lack of independent witnesses.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The crime was a brutal and heinous act, involving the killing of five persons in a violent and cruel manner. The accused formed an unlawful assembly with a common object to kill the deceased persons.
other_sentence_order: The High Court's decision to commute the death sentence to life imprisonment was upheld. The Court also affirmed the acquittals of some accused persons based on the High Court's reasonable analysis of the evidence.
